formation.title: The Old North Reborn
formation.text:
The disparate Brythonic kingdoms of the north (Rheged, Gododdin, Strathclyde, Elmet) have been reunited under a single crown for the first time since the age of Urien and Taliesin. The Cumbric tongue is spoken from the Firth of Forth to the Humber, and the old genealogies of the Gwyr y Gogledd bind this realm together.

But what kind of realm shall this be? The bards who preserved the memory of the Old North through centuries of Saxon and Norse domination now look to us for guidance. Shall we be the guardians of an ancient culture reborn, nurturing the poetic and legal traditions that make us distinct? Or shall we be the avengers of Catraeth, wielding the sword to carve out a kingdom worthy of Urien's legacy?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Let the Awen guide us: we are keepers of the flame

modifiers.name: Yr Awen
modifiers.text: The divine poetic inspiration flows through the bards of the Old North once more. Where the Cynfeirdd once sang of heroes, a new generation preserves the Cumbric tongue and the ancient laws of the Brythonic people.

options.text: The Sword of the North shall not rest in its scabbard

modifiers.name: Cleddyf y Gogledd
modifiers.text: The Sword of the North is drawn again. As Urien once drove the Angles from the shores of Lindisfarne, the warriors of Hen Ogledd march to reclaim every hill and valley that was once Brythonic.

advances.name: Y Gododdin
advances.text: The ancient poem of Aneirin commemorating the Brythonic warriors who fell at the Battle of Catraeth inspires the soldiers of Hen Ogledd with tales of selfless valor.

event.title: Y Gododdin
event.text:
In the great hall, by firelight, a bard rises to recite the oldest and most sacred verses of the Brythonic people. Y Gododdin: the elegy of Aneirin for the three hundred warriors who rode from Din Eidyn to Catraeth, there to fight against overwhelming Anglian numbers. Nearly all were slain, yet their names live on in immortal verse.

The poem's opening lines are known to every warrior in the realm: 'Gwyr a aeth Gatraeth oedd ffraeth eu llu': 'Men went to Catraeth, keen was their host.' It is not merely a memorial but a sacred bond between past and present, reminding all who hear it that courage in the face of destruction is the highest virtue of the Old North.

Tonight, the warriors who listen vow to be worthy of those ancient heroes.

options.text: Their sacrifice will never be forgotten

modifiers.name: The Heroes of Catraeth
modifiers.text: The verses of Y Gododdin echo in every hall. Three hundred went to Catraeth and nearly all fell, but their sacrifice has become the immortal standard by which all warriors of the Old North are measured.

advances.name: The Gosgordd
advances.text: The king's personal warband of mounted retainers, bound by oath and kinship, forms the elite core of the Brythonic military tradition.

advances.name: Lords of the Herds
advances.text: The pastoral cattle economy of the Brythonic north, where wealth is measured in livestock and the royal court's power flows from its herds.

advances.name: The Cynfeirdd
advances.text: The earliest poets (Taliesin and Aneirin foremost among them) who sang the deeds of Brythonic kings and preserved the cultural identity of the Old North through centuries of conflict.

advances.name: Cumbric Law
advances.text: The legal customs of the Brythonic north, blending ancient tribal practice with remnants of Roman administration into a distinctive jurisprudence.

advances.name: Alt Clut
advances.text: The Rock of the Clyde, Dumbarton Rock, where Brythonic kings have held court since the departure of the Roman legions. Its basalt summit has resisted siege for centuries.

event.title: The Rock of the Clyde
event.text:
Dumbarton Rock (Alt Clut in the old tongue, the Rock of the Clyde) has been the seat of Brythonic power in the north since before memory. Rising two hundred and forty feet above the river, its basalt summit has never been taken by direct assault. When the Norse kings Amlaib and Imar besieged it in 870, they required four months and the cutting of its water supply to force its submission.

Now the fortress has been expanded and reinforced with the latest defensive works. A new curtain wall encircles the summit, and the garrison has been doubled. From this impregnable perch, the rulers of Hen Ogledd can command the entire course of the Clyde and control all movement between the Scottish Lowlands and the western sea.

modifiers.name: Rock of the Clyde
modifiers.text: Alt Clut stands once more as the impregnable seat of Brythonic power. Where Dumbarton Rock rises above the river, no invader can pass unchallenged.

advances.name: Brythonic Smithcraft
advances.text: The metalworkers of the Old North produce fine swords, shields, and torcs in a tradition stretching back to the Iron Age Britons. The gof keeps his forge under the protection of the law.

advances.name: Clyde Trade
advances.text: The River Clyde serves as the commercial artery of the western Old North, connecting the interior with Irish and continental traders. Hides tanned in the bark houses along its banks go downriver as leather.

advances.name: The Cumbric Church
advances.text: The Christianity of the Old North follows insular traditions distinct from both Rome and Canterbury, with its own monastic practices and calendar.

advances.name: Frontier Spearmen
advances.text: The borderlands of Hen Ogledd breed disciplined spearmen hardened by constant frontier warfare against Angles, Gaels, and Norse.

advances.name: Northern Wool Trade
advances.text: The upland pastures of the Pennines and Southern Uplands produce high-quality wool, which Brythonic weavers transform into sought-after cloth. Fulling mills are raised on the upland streams.

advances.name: The Northern Alliance
advances.text: Following Urien of Rheged's example of forging coalitions among Brythonic kings against the common enemy, the Old North masters the art of alliance diplomacy.

advances.name: Border Strongholds
advances.text: A network of hilltop fortifications guards the marches of Hen Ogledd, each stronghold mutually supporting its neighbors and controlling the passes.

advances.name: Manuscript Tradition
advances.text:
The bardic halls of the Old North produce illuminated manuscripts preserving the poetry, laws, and histories of the Brythonic people for posterity.

Available in: Neuadd y Beirdd

advances.name: Border Riders
advances.text: Swift mounted raiders who patrol the frontier marches, expert at hit-and-run tactics in the broken terrain of the border country.

advances.name: Bardic Preservation
advances.text: The bardic schools of the Old North systematically preserve and teach the Cumbric language, ensuring the oral traditions and legal codes survive the pressure of surrounding cultures.

advances.name: Kingdom Reunited
advances.text: The separate Brythonic kingdoms of the north are consolidated under a single crown, ending centuries of fragmentation and bringing the vision of a unified Old North to fruition.

advances.name: Pennine Mines
advances.text: The lead and coal deposits of the Pennine hills have been exploited since Roman times. Under Brythonic governance, organized mining brings new wealth to the Old North. Bole hearths are lit on the windy brows above the ore fields.

advances.name: Milwyr y Gogledd
advances.text: The old teulu warband system gives way to a permanent standing army (the Soldiers of the North) trained and equipped to modern standards while retaining the martial spirit of the Gododdin warriors.

advances.name: Coastal Commerce
advances.text: The ports of the Clyde, Solway, and Northumbrian coast develop into thriving centers of coastal and cross-channel trade with Ireland, Scandinavia, and the continent.

advances.name: Council of the North
advances.text: Drawing on Brythonic traditions of counsel and consent, a formal council advises the crown and shapes the governance of the realm.

advances.name: Northern Industry
advances.text:
The coalfields and iron deposits of the Old North support a growing proto-industrial economy, forging weapons, tools, and the material foundations of modern power.

Available in: Gefail

advances.name: Cumbric Revival
advances.text: A literary and cultural renaissance reclaims the Cumbric language from centuries of marginalization, producing new poetry, histories, and legal texts inspired by the Cynfeirdd tradition.

advances.name: Industrial North
advances.text: The northern coalfields and river valleys become the heartland of an industrial revolution, with mills, foundries, and factories transforming the landscape of Hen Ogledd.

advances.name: Clyde Shipyards
advances.text: The banks of the River Clyde, once home to simple fishing villages, now host great shipyards that launch vessels for trade and war across the world's oceans.

advances.name: Democratic Tradition
advances.text: The ancient Brythonic practice of governance by counsel and consent evolves into a modern democratic tradition, giving voice to the common people of the Old North.

destiny.name: The Old North Consolidated
destiny.text: The Brythonic kingdoms have been reunited under one crown. Stability must be maintained before the realm can pursue its greater destiny.

event.title: The Old North Consolidated
event.text:
Hen Ogledd stands firm. The old kingdoms of Rheged, Gododdin, and Strathclyde answer to a single crown for the first time in centuries. The realm is stable, the borders are secured, and the people look to their king for direction.

The question that has haunted the Brythonic north since the fall of the Roman order is answered at last: the Old North endures. Now comes the harder question: what shall it become?

destiny.name: Schools of the Cynfeirdd
destiny.text: Establish centers of Brythonic learning by raising bardic halls in two towns and securing a supply of paper for the scribes and scholars who will carry the Cumbric tradition forward.

conditions.text: At least 2 of our locations have a Neuadd y Beirdd

children.text: Paper is produced in the market
Paper is traded in the market

event.title: Schools of the Cynfeirdd
event.text:
Across the realm, the schools of the Cynfeirdd have been transformed. What were once informal gatherings of bards passing down oral traditions have become organized institutions of learning. Young scholars now study not only the intricate meters of Cumbric poetry but also philosophy, law, mathematics, and the natural sciences.

Paper (once a rare luxury) flows through the markets of the Old North. The works of Taliesin and Aneirin are copied, studied, and expanded upon. New treatises in the Cumbric tongue rival anything produced in Latin or French. The intellectual foundations of a Brythonic renaissance have been laid.

options.text: The Awen illuminates all who seek knowledge

destiny.name: The Brythonic Union
destiny.text: Reunite with the Welsh Brythons by taking Carmarthen, the ancient seat of Deheubarth. Teach one in five of the realm's people to read, so that Cumbric and Welsh books find readers, gather the gold to fund the project, and all Brythonic peoples can be gathered under one banner.

event.title: The Brythonic Union
event.text:
Carmarthen has fallen to us, or rather, returned to us. The ancient seat of Deheubarth, the heartland of Welsh Brythonic civilization, is united with the Old North for the first time since the post-Roman era. The scholars of the north and the bards of Wales find that they share more than a common linguistic ancestor: they share a vision of Brythonic civilization restored.

The printing press now carries Cumbric and Welsh texts to every corner of the realm. But how shall we channel this cultural momentum? Through great gatherings of poets and scholars that celebrate our shared heritage? Or through the restoration of the ancient Brythonic legal codes that once governed all Prydain?

options.text: Convene the Eisteddfod: a festival of arts

modifiers.name: The Eisteddfod
modifiers.text: Great festivals of poetry, music, and scholarship draw artists from across the Brythonic world, spreading cultural influence and healing the scars of centuries of conflict.

options.text: Restore the Cyfraith: the law of the Britons

modifiers.name: Cyfraith y Brythoniaid
modifiers.text: The ancient legal codes of the Britons have been restored and codified, providing a just and tolerant framework for governing a diverse people.

destiny.name: Prifysgol y Gogledd
destiny.text: Found the University of the North, a great center of Brythonic scholarship rivaling any in Europe. This requires Glasgow, the see of Kentigern, held and built up to twice what it was, high prestige, and bardic halls in four towns from which its masters are drawn.

conditions.text: Glasgow is owned directly and has at least 46 development

event.title: Prifysgol y Gogledd
event.text:
The University of the North opens its doors. Built in the Brythonic scholarly tradition but embracing the new learning the presses carry across Europe, it stands as proof that a language once dismissed as the speech of herdsmen and cattle-raiders can serve as the medium for the highest learning.

Scholars from across the Celtic world (Wales, Ireland, Cornwall, Brittany) flock to the Prifysgol. The question now is what shall define this institution's character. Shall it look outward, building networks of trade and diplomacy that carry Brythonic ideas across Europe? Or shall it look inward, nurturing the poetic and literary traditions that make the Cumbric world unique?

options.text: Outward: let our scholars walk among the nations

modifiers.name: Enlightened North
modifiers.text: The scholars of Prifysgol y Gogledd build networks across Europe, carrying Brythonic ideas into the wider world and bringing back trade and diplomatic connections.

options.text: Inward: let the Awen speak through a new age

modifiers.name: The Age of Verse
modifiers.text: A golden age of Cumbric poetry and song. The bardic tradition reaches heights not seen since Taliesin, and the cultural prestige of the Brythonic world draws converts and admirers.

destiny.name: Caer Ludd
destiny.text: Take London (Caer Ludd in the old tongue, the city founded by King Lud according to Brythonic legend). The old road south from York runs through Lincoln, which must be held as well.

conditions.text: Chose the Cleddyf y Gogledd destiny

event.title: The Fall of London
event.text:
Caer Ludd has fallen. London (the greatest city in England, the heart of Anglo-Saxon power) flies the banner of Hen Ogledd. The city that the Brythonic Britons lost to the Saxons in the dark centuries after Rome has been reclaimed by their descendants.

According to Geoffrey of Monmouth, London was founded by King Lud, who named it Caer Ludd. Whether the legend is true matters less than what it represents: the city belongs to the Britons by right of ancient inheritance. The warriors of the Old North march through streets that their ancestors last walked a thousand years ago.

The Anglo-Saxon chroniclers wrote that the Britons fled westward forever. They were wrong.

options.text: Caer Ludd is ours once more

destiny.name: Masters of the Celtic Seas
destiny.text: Control the Irish Sea by taking Dublin and Cornwall, linking the Celtic peoples of Ireland, Wales, and the Old North under Brythonic dominion.

event.title: Masters of the Celtic Seas
event.text:
Dublin and Cornwall are ours. The Irish Sea is now a Brythonic lake, and the Celtic peoples of three islands (Britain, Ireland, and the scattered Atlantic communities) look to the Old North as their champion.

But the nature of this hegemony remains to be determined. Shall we forge a confederation of Celtic peoples, binding them through alliance and shared purpose while respecting their distinct identities? Or shall we fortify our island domains into an impregnable bastion, making Britain itself the greatest fortress in the world?

modifiers.name: Celtic Alliance
modifiers.text: A confederation of Celtic peoples under Brythonic leadership, bound by shared language and purpose. Subject nations are loyal partners, not conquered provinces.

modifiers.name: Island Fortress
modifiers.text: Britain has been fortified into an impregnable bastion. The land provides for its own defense, though the fortress mentality constrains outward trade.

destiny.name: Sons of Brutus
destiny.text: According to Geoffrey of Monmouth, the Britons descend from Brutus of Troy. Reach across the Channel to Rouen in Normandy and to Rennes, claiming kinship with the Bretons and dominion over both shores. This is the apex of Brythonic military power.

event.title: Sons of Brutus
event.text:
Rouen has fallen. The banner of Hen Ogledd flies on the continent. The Brythonic people, who retreated from Brittany to the margins of Britain, have returned to claim their ancient kinship with the Bretons, and more.

Geoffrey of Monmouth wrote that Brutus of Troy founded Britain and gave it his name. Whether myth or memory, the claim carries weight: the Britons have proven that they are a people of destiny, capable of conquering not merely an island but reaching across the sea. The question now is how to wield this unprecedented power.

options.text: In the spirit of Urien: conquest and glory

modifiers.name: Urien Reborn
modifiers.text: The spirit of Urien of Rheged lives again in a conquering king. The armies of the Old North are disciplined and vast, though endless campaigning strains the treasury.

options.text: A Celtic empire bound by blood and tongue

modifiers.name: Celtic Empire
modifiers.text: A pan-Celtic realm stretching from Scotland to Brittany, bound by blood and tongue. The power to dictate peace terms comes at the cost of perpetual readiness for war.

units.name: Gosgordd
units.text: The king's personal warband of mounted retainers, the gosgordd ride as the elite shock cavalry of the Old North. Bound by oaths of loyalty and inspired by the heroes of Y Gododdin, they charge with reckless valor.

units.name: Gosgordd
units.text: The frontier spearmen of Hen Ogledd, the gosgordd are hardened infantry trained in the broken terrain of the border marches. They excel at holding ground against superior numbers in hills and mountain passes.

units.name: Border Rider
units.text: Swift mounted raiders who know every pass, ford, and hidden valley of the frontier country. They strike fast, loot quickly, and vanish before the enemy can mount a response.

units.name: Milwyr y Gogledd
units.text: The Soldiers of the North, a disciplined standing infantry force that replaces the old warband levies with professional troops equipped with modern weapons and tactics.

buildings.name: Llys
buildings.text: The royal court-hall of a Brythonic king, where justice is dispensed, cattle tribute is collected, and the bards sing the genealogies of the ruling house.

buildings.name: Neuadd y Beirdd
buildings.text: The Bardic Hall, where the poetic traditions of Taliesin and Aneirin are taught to new generations and the Cumbric language is preserved through verse and song.

buildings.name: Dinas
buildings.text: A hilltop fortress in the Brythonic tradition, commanding the surrounding countryside from an elevated position. Built on natural rock outcrops, these strongholds are nearly impervious to assault.

buildings.name: Gefail
buildings.text: The forge of the gof. In Brythonic law smithcraft is one of the three arts a bondsman's son may not learn without his lord's leave, and the court smith is an officer of the king's household.

buildings.name: Barcdy
buildings.text: The bark house, a tannery on the river bank. Hides lie in pits of oak bark and running water before they are carried downriver.

buildings.name: Pandy
buildings.text: The fulling mill on an upland stream. A water wheel lifts the hammers that beat and thicken the web.

buildings.name: Bole Hill
buildings.text: A smelting hearth on a windy brow of the ore field. Lead ore and brushwood are stacked in a ring of stones, and the west wind does the work of bellows.

where.text: The location's raw material is Lead

buildings.name: Prifysgol y Gogledd
buildings.text: The University of the North, a great center of Brythonic learning where the bardic tradition meets the new science. Scholars from across the Celtic world study poetry, law, natural philosophy, and mathematics in the Cumbric tongue.

buildings.name: Caer Ludd
buildings.text: The legendary Brythonic fortress of London, rebuilt as the military citadel of a conquering Celtic people. Its massive walls and garrison command the Thames and the surrounding countryside.

list.name: Cyfraith Hywel
list.text: The Welsh law code attributed to Hywel Dda in the mid-tenth century, preserved in the Iorwerth, Cyfnerth, and Blegywryd redactions. It codifies galanas (kindred blood-price), sarhad (insult-fine), and mach (sworn surety), administered through cwmwd courts of uchelwyr. The clergy preserved the manuscripts; the laws favoured graded fines over feud, which the great kindreds resented.

list.name: Llys a Maerdref
list.text: The royal court (llys) and its bound demesne village (maerdref), where taeogion bondsmen farmed the king's table-land and the maer collected dawnbwyd food-renders. The king progressed his cylch circuit through the maerdrefi, consuming renders in person. Itinerant kingship sustained the warband on the move but bound the bondsmen to the soil for generations.

list.name: Penteulu
list.text: The captain of the king's mounted warband (teulu), second-ranked officer of the court after the edling. The teulu of one hundred and twenty oath-bound retainers, drawn from noble households, served as the king's strike force and bodyguard. Y Gododdin commemorates such a warband, the three hundred who rode south to die at Catraeth.

list.name: Bardd Teulu a Phencerdd
list.text: The bardic order, formally graded by the Laws of Hywel into pencerdd (master bard, paid by chair competition), bardd teulu (war-band poet sung before battle), and lesser cerddorion. Bards preserved the genealogies of kings, sang the praises of the dynasty, and could legitimate or unmake a ruler with their verse. Their tongue was Cumbric, and through them the Brythonic tongue carried weight beyond the borders.

list.name: Cwmwd Court System
list.text: Each cwmwd was an autonomous legal-territorial unit of half or a third of a cantref, with its own court of uchelwyr presided over by a rhaglaw (legal officer) and policed by a rhingyll (bailiff). By the thirteenth century the cwmwd court had eclipsed the cantref court as the primary venue for Welsh law. Local justice, local power, and a thousand local lords.

list.name: Clas Communities
list.text: Mother churches of the Brythonic Christian tradition, administered by hereditary clerical kindreds where the abbacy passed from father to son or uncle to nephew. Govan, Glasgow, and the clasau of Cumbria served as religious-administrative centres for wide territories. Their hereditary character preserved Brythonic learning but resisted Roman reform; clergy and noble kindreds intermarried freely.

list.name: Galanas Kindred Liability
list.text: Under Cyfraith Hywel the cenedl (the four-generation paternal kindred) was the unit of legal liability. Galanas blood-price for homicide was paid and received collectively, with the table graduated by status. Crime was settled between cenedlau, not between subject and king. The kindreds protected their own; the throne, lacking a monopoly on justice, learned to govern through them rather than over them.
